title: Colours, مَا الْمَوْصُولَة, and the Door Opens: ثُلَاثِي مُجَرَّد versus ثُلَاثِي مَزِيد فِيهِ
summary: The shopping-list dialogue of lesson sixteen supplies the masculine and feminine patterns of the colours, غَيْر as a permanent مُضَاف, آخَر with its feminine أُخْرَى, and مَا الْمَوْصُولَة as a third kind of مَا. The session then turns to what the teacher calls the game changer: until now every verb had three root letters and nothing more, but أَرَادَ يُرِيدُ belongs to a second class, ثُلَاثِي مَزِيد فِيهِ, where letters are added to the root. He opens two of its ten patterns — فَعَّلَ and أَفْعَلَ — each with its own مَصْدَر.
key_points: The colours take the pattern أَفْعَل in the masculine — أَحْمَر (red), أَبْيَض (white), أَسْوَد (black), أَصْفَر (yellow), أَزْرَق (blue), أَسْمَر (brown) — and فَعْلَاء in the feminine: حَمْرَاء، بَيْضَاء، سَوْدَاء، صَفْرَاء.
The colour must match what it describes, so a حَقِيبَة, being feminine, is حَقِيبَةٌ حَمْرَاءُ, never أَحْمَر.
غَيْر means not and is almost always مُضَاف to what follows: غَيْر مُسْلِم (not a Muslim), غَيْر مُسَطَّر (unlined), and غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ in Sūrat al-Fātiḥah.
آخَر means another, with the feminine أُخْرَى — hence مَرَّةً أُخْرَى, another time.

مَا الْمَوْصُولَة is a third type of مَا, after الِاسْتِفْهَامِيَّة (questioning) and النَّافِيَة (negating). It means that or which and does the same work as الَّذِي — لَا أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ, I do not worship that which you worship. It belongs to the اسْم الْمَوْصُول family.

The verbs met so far are ثُلَاثِي مُجَرَّد (thulāthī mujarrad): three root letters with nothing added, so the مَاضِي has three letters (ذَهَبَ) and the مُضَارِع four (يَذْهَبُ), the extra letter being only the prefix of the present tense.
ثُلَاثِي مَزِيد فِيهِ (thulāthī mazīd fīhi) still has three root letters but with something added — from زَادَ، يَزِيدُ, to increase. There are ten such patterns in all.

The first pattern: فَعَّلَ، يُفَعِّلُ, whose مَصْدَر is تَفْعِيل. The shadda is itself an added letter, since فَعَّلَ is really فَعْعَلَ with two identical letters merged. Examples: فَصَّلَ، يُفَصِّلُ; كَبَّرَ، يُكَبِّرُ، تَكْبِير; سَبَّحَ، يُسَبِّحُ، تَسْبِيح.
The second pattern: أَفْعَلَ، يُفْعِلُ, whose مَصْدَر is إِفْعَال. Examples: أَكْرَمَ، يُكْرِمُ، إِكْرَام; أَسْلَمَ، يُسْلِمُ، إِسْلَام; أَسْمَعَ، يُسْمِعُ.
Each added pattern carries its own shade of meaning: سَمِعَ is to hear, while أَسْمَعَ is to make someone hear. The specifics come later.
أَرَادَ، يُرِيدُ belongs to the أَفْعَلَ pattern, which is why its مُضَارِع prefix carries a ḍamma rather than the familiar fatḥa — يُرِيدُ، أُرِيدُ، نُرِيدُ، تُرِيدِينَ.
The same system explains familiar words: مُسْلِم is the doer of أَسْلَمَ، يُسْلِمُ, and إِسْلَام is its مَصْدَر.
مُصْحَف is the correct word for the physical book; الْقُرْآن is the speech of Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ itself. So one should ask for a مُصْحَف rather than say buy me a Qur'ān.
يَا أَبَتِ is a more affectionate and respectful way of addressing a father than يَا أَبِي, and it is how Yūsuf, Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīل عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَام address their fathers in the Qur'ān.

Vocabulary: مُسَطَّر (lined) from سَطْر (a line), حَلْوَى (sweets), مِلَفّ (folder), مُعْجَم (dictionary), نَمُوذَج (sample or blueprint), قُمَاش (cloth or fabric), مِتْر with its plural أَمْتَار, اِشْتَرَى (to buy), and حَرْف (letter).
questions: [00:02:01] Q: Why does يُرِيدُ have a ḍamma on its prefix instead of the usual fatḥa? — A: Because it belongs to a different, added pattern of the verb — أَرَادَ، يُرِيدُ on the أَفْعَلَ form, not the plain three-letter type.
[00:04:00] Q: Why is it أَحْمَرَ in that phrase? — A: Because it is the صِفَة of قَلَمًا and must follow it in case.
[00:05:00] Q: Are عَمْرو and عُمَر the same name? — A: No, they are separate names. A wāw is written in عَمْرو to distinguish it, since without it a reader could not tell the two apart.
[00:14:00] Q: Why is it حَقِيبَةٌ حَمْرَاءُ and not أَحْمَر? — A: Because حَقِيبَة is feminine, so the colour takes its feminine pattern, فَعْلَاء.

[00:16:00] Q: Does مُصْحَف mean notebook? — A: No. The مُصْحَف is the bound book containing the Qur'ān; الْقُرْآن is the speech of Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ, which is why saying buy me a Qur'ān is imprecise.

[00:19:00] Q: Why did she answer بَلَى rather than نَعَمْ? — A: The question was do you not want anything; نَعَمْ would have confirmed that she wants nothing, so بَلَى negates the negative to say that she does.
[00:24:00] Q: What are the three types of مَا we now have? — A: الِاسْتِفْهَامِيَّة for questions, النَّافِيَة for negating, and الْمَوْصُولَة meaning that or which.
[00:25:00] Q: Which family does this مَا belong to? — A: الِاسْم الْمَوْصُول, the same family as الَّذِي and الَّتِي, though used in different contexts.

[00:33:02] Q: فَعَّلَ still looks like three letters, so what has been added? — A: The shadda. A shadda is two identical letters merged, so يُفَعِّلُ is really يُفَعْعِلُ — the doubled letter is the addition.

quiz.q: On which pattern are the masculine colours built?
quiz.a: أَحْمَر، أَبْيَض، أَسْوَد، أَصْفَر، أَزْرَق all follow أَفْعَل.
حَمْرَاء، بَيْضَاء، سَوْدَاء، صَفْرَاء — the pattern in بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَاءُ.

options: It takes a verb after it
It is مُضَاف to the following word
quiz.a: غَيْر مُسَطَّر، غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ — the following noun is its مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ.

quiz.q: What is the feminine of آخَر?
quiz.a: أُخْرَى, as in مَرَّةً أُخْرَى, another time.

quiz.q: What does مَا الْمَوْصُولَة mean, and what is it equivalent to?
options: What — equivalent to a question word
That or which — equivalent to الَّذِي
quiz.a: لَا أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ — I do not worship that which you worship; it works like الَّذِي.

options: Three root letters with nothing added
quiz.a: ثُلَاثِي for the three root letters, مُجَرَّد meaning bare — ذَهَبَ، يَذْهَبُ, where the only extra letter is the present-tense prefix.

quiz.q: What is the مَصْدَر pattern of فَعَّلَ، يُفَعِّلُ?
quiz.a: تَفْعِيل — كَبَّرَ gives تَكْبِير, and سَبَّحَ gives تَسْبِيح.

quiz.q: What is the مَصْدَر pattern of أَفْعَلَ، يُفْعِلُ?
quiz.a: إِفْعَال — أَكْرَمَ gives إِكْرَام, and أَسْلَمَ gives إِسْلَام.

quiz.q: What does أَسْمَعَ mean, as against سَمِعَ?
options: سَمِعَ is to hear; أَسْمَعَ is to make someone hear
quiz.a: Each added pattern carries its own shade of meaning, and أَفْعَلَ here makes the action causative.

quiz.q: What is the correct word for the physical book containing the Qur'ān?
quiz.a: الْقُرْآن is the speech of Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ itself; the bound volume is the مُصْحَف.

quran_examples.arabic: إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَاءُ فَاقِعٌ لَّوْنُهَا تَسُرُّ النَّاظِرِينَ
quran_examples.transliteration: innahu yaqūlu innahā baqaratun ṣafrāʾu fāqiʿun lawnuhā tasurru al-nāẓirīn
quran_examples.translation: He says it is a yellow cow, bright in colour, pleasing to the beholders.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example for the feminine colour pattern: صَفْرَاء is the feminine of أَصْفَر, agreeing with بَقَرَة.

quran_examples.translation: White and delicious to the drinkers.
quran_examples.note: A second feminine colour on the same pattern, بَيْضَاء from أَبْيَض, describing the drink of Paradise.

quran_examples.arabic: صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ
quran_examples.transliteration: ṣirāṭa alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim ghayri al-maghḍūbi ʿalayhim wa-lā al-ḍāllīn
quran_examples.translation: The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have earned Your anger, nor of those who go astray.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's illustration of غَيْر as a مُضَاف — a construction recited daily.

quran_examples.translation: I do not worship what you worship.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example of مَا الْمَوْصُولَة standing in for الَّذِي — that which you worship — alongside لَا النَّافِيَة in the same clause.

quran_examples.arabic: لَا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا آخَرَ فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَّخْذُولًا
quran_examples.transliteration: lā tajʿal maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhara fa-taqʿuda madhmūman makhdhūlā
quran_examples.translation: Do not set up with Allah another deity, lest you end up blamed and forsaken.
quran_examples.note: Cited for آخَر meaning another; it is also a singular نَهْي, carrying the jazm from the previous lessons.

quran_examples.arabic: وَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَدًا وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي الْمُلْكِ ۖ وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًا
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-quli al-ḥamdu li-llāhi alladhī lam yattakhidh waladan wa-lam yakun lahu sharīkun fī al-mulk, wa-kabbirhu takbīrā
quran_examples.translation: And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son and has no partner in dominion; and magnify Him with all magnificence.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example for the فَعَّلَ pattern and its مَصْدَر together: the command كَبِّرْ with تَكْبِيرًا in the same phrase.

quran_examples.arabic: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
quran_examples.transliteration: sabbaḥa li-llāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ, wa-huwa al-ʿazīzu al-ḥakīm
quran_examples.translation: Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
quran_examples.note: سَبَّحَ on the فَعَّلَ pattern, whose مَصْدَر تَسْبِيح the class already knew — and مَا here is الْمَوْصُولَة, whatever is in the heavens.

quran_examples.translation: They were slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive.
quran_examples.note: A student's answer for the فَعَّلَ pattern in the present tense; the teacher used it to show that the shadda in يُذَبِّحُ is an added letter.

quran_examples.translation: Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example for the أَفْعَلَ pattern: تُسْمِعُ is not to hear but to make hear, as distinct from سَمِعَ.

quran_examples.arabic: بَلَىٰ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ فَلَهُ أَجْرُهُ عِندَ رَبِّهِ
quran_examples.transliteration: balā man aslama wajhahu li-llāhi wa-huwa muḥsinun fa-lahu ajruhu ʿinda rabbih
quran_examples.translation: Yes indeed — whoever submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good will have his reward with his Lord.
quran_examples.note: أَسْلَمَ on the أَفْعَلَ pattern, from which come both إِسْلَام as its مَصْدَر and مُسْلِم as its doer — the teacher's point that the system explains words the class already knew. It also opens with بَلَى.

quran_examples.arabic: يَا أَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لِي سَاجِدِينَ
quran_examples.transliteration: yā abati innī raʾaytu aḥada ʿashara kawkaban wa-l-shamsa wa-l-qamara lī sājidīn
quran_examples.translation: O my father, I have seen eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.
quran_examples.note: The affectionate يَا أَبَتِ the teacher pointed out in the speech of the prophets — and أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا is the eleven-form with its singular مَعْدُود in the accusative, exactly as drilled earlier.
